title: Symphony No. 7 in C major
hook: A whole symphony in one span of about twenty minutes, and Sibelius’s last.

painting.title: Kaukola Ridge at Sunset
painting.collection: Finnish National Gallery, Ateneum Art Museum, Helsinki
painting.pairingNote: Finnish lakes and forest under a golden evening light, seen from a height in one long sweep; the Seventh, too, is one long span that ends in a blaze of C major.

facts: Sibelius first mentioned the Seventh in his diary in December 1917, while still revising the Fifth. In 1918 he imagined it in three movements, full of “joy of life and vitality”; in the early 1920s he planned four. Most of the music came from the planned slow movement, and around 1923 he decided to fuse everything into a single movement.

He finished the score on 2 March 1924, often working at night, and conducted the premiere himself in Stockholm on 24 March 1924, with the orchestra of the Stockholm Konsertförening. At first he called it *Fantasia sinfonica*; only later, when it was published, did it become Symphony No. 7.

It lasts a little over twenty minutes and never stops. The tempo keeps changing, slowly and almost imperceptibly, from a slow beginning to fast dance-like music and back. Three times a noble trombone theme rises above the orchestra, and these three moments are the pillars of the whole work.
It was his last symphony. He worked on an Eighth for years but destroyed it, and after the tone poem *Tapiola* (1926) he wrote little more of significance in the three decades he still lived.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a slow rising, a hymn in the strings and the first trombone theme; a quickening into a storm and the trombone again, in C minor; a dance that speeds up into the third trombone theme, in C major, and a final chord.

movements.heading: Symphony No. 7
movements.tempo: Adagio – Vivacissimo – Allegro molto moderato – Presto – Adagio
movements.summary: One continuous movement. It begins with a slow scale climbing in the strings, settles into a long, hymn-like passage for divided strings, and brings in a majestic trombone theme. The music then speeds up, little by little, into a stormy passage where the trombone returns in the minor; lightens into a dance; speeds up again; and reaches the trombone theme a third time, in full glory. Memories of the opening lead to the final chord.

mainIdeas.name: The rising scale
mainIdeas.description: a slow climb in the strings that opens the symphony.

mainIdeas.name: The hymn
mainIdeas.description: a long, many-voiced passage for the strings alone, like a chorale.

mainIdeas.name: The trombone theme
mainIdeas.description: a broad, noble melody for solo trombone, heard three times.

mainIdeas.name: The dance
mainIdeas.description: a lighter, swinging passage in the middle of the work.

stops.hear: A soft timpani stroke; the strings climb slowly up a scale
A flute sings a short, plaintive phrase; woodwind answer with a little falling and rising figure
The strings, divided into many parts, play a slow, rich, hymn-like passage
stops.happening: The string chorale; Sibelius said it was “as if before the face of God”

stops.hear: The music gathers strength and rises
stops.happening: The approach to the first summit

stops.hear: A solo trombone rises above the orchestra with a broad, noble melody
stops.happening: The trombone theme, in C major (first time)

stops.hear: The pulse begins to quicken, so gradually that it is hard to say when
Fast, swirling string figures, like wind
The trombone theme returns, now dark and stormy

The dance speeds up, more and more

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The strings climb to the final note and a great C major chord fills the space

notice: Try to catch the moment when the tempo changes. Sibelius makes each change gradual, so that you notice only afterwards that the music is moving faster or slower.
Listen for the three appearances of the trombone theme: majestic, then stormy, then triumphant. They are the landmarks of the whole symphony.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Osmo Vänskä and the Lahti Symphony Orchestra recorded all of Sibelius’s symphonies for the Swedish label BIS in the 1990s, together with the first recordings of the original versions of the Fifth Symphony and the Violin Concerto. Like all the orchestra’s recordings, this one was made in Alvar Aalto’s Church of the Cross in Lahti. On the Spotify album the Seventh is track 5, between the Sixth Symphony and *Tapiola*.

threads.title: One span
threads.body: There are no breaks and no separate movements. Slow, fast and dance-like music flow into each other, and the tempo changes are gradual.

threads.title: The trombone
threads.body: One theme, on one instrument, holds the work together: it appears three times, in three moods.

threads.title: C major
threads.body: The symphony begins and ends in C major, the plainest of keys; the last chord sounds like an arrival.

threads.title: An ending
threads.body: It was Sibelius’s last symphony, though he lived until 1957.
